lines.trans: Are you heading to the station?
No, I am going to the hospital—today is the day my stitches come out.
Hop in—my meeting starts at lunchtime, so I can go in a little late.
Hey, why do you keep tidying up when it is already clean? It is way cleaner than my car.
Huh? Is that not someone I know?
Yes, Director, I got the contact info. I will call you the moment we arrive at the airport.
Honestly, even I think CEO Byun is going too far—making a girl in a cast do an event.
Still, what can we do—let us get back and rest. I will push back strongly for you too.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Used as honorific polite imperative (가세요!).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (go safely)
Let us do that (go (honorific)) right away.

meanings.note: Used as adverbial -게 (강력하게).

examples.text: 그래도 어쩌냐, 갔다 와서 좀 쉬자. 오빠도 강력하게 어필해볼게.
examples.trans: Still, what can we do—let us get back and rest. I will push back strongly for you too.

examples.trans: All the reporters waiting out there to shoot her airport fashion came up empty-handed.

meanings.note: Used as noun + -까지 (깁스까지).

examples.text: 나도 솔직히 좀 대표님이 너무하신다고 생각한다. 아니, 깁스까지 한 애한테 행사라니.
examples.trans: Honestly, even I think CEO Byun is going too far—making a girl in a cast do an event.

meanings.note: Used as contrastive -은데 (깨끗한데).

examples.text: 야, 뭘 깨끗한데 계속 치워? 내 차보다 훨씬 깨끗하다.
examples.trans: Hey, why do you keep tidying up when it is already clean? It is way cleaner than my car.
It is really when it is clean compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 술 많이 마신 날엔 밀가루 안 먹는다고 했는데 삼선짜장을 시키셔서, 어제 생각보다 많이 마신 건 아니지 않을까요?
examples.trans: He once said he avoids flour after heavy drinking yet ordered black-bean noodles—might he have drunk less than we thought?
Here the word for 'on days when' is key.
The atmosphere today is really was too much.
That person always looks was too much.

meanings.en: to be late, to be behind schedule
meanings.note: Takes attributive -은 (늦은) before a noun.

examples.trans: I was a little late today.
Sorry for the late hour.
Did you hear about this just as?
I was busy today because of just as.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

examples.text: 조금만 더 가면 금방 도착할 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: If we go just a little farther, we should arrive soon.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 도착하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (will arrive).

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to emphasize immediate action or result.
E.g., 바로 옆 ('right next to'), 바로 그 사람 ('that very person').

examples.trans: I'll start right away now.
The cafe is right in front of the school.

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

examples.text: 네 매형 병원이 요새 되게 힘들다.
examples.trans: Your brother-in-law's clinic is having a really hard time lately.

examples.text: 병원 문 닫고 네 매형 백수 되게 생겼다니까.
examples.trans: The clinic is about to close and turn your brother-in-law into an unemployed man.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?
Oh? It is raining.

examples.trans: Still, what can we do—let us get back and rest. I will push back strongly for you too.

meanings.note: Used as humble volitional formal (연락드리겠습니다.).

examples.text: 예, 실장님 연락처 받았습니다. 공항 도착하는 대로 바로 연락드리겠습니다.

meanings.note: Used as noun (연락처).

examples.trans: Yes, Director, I got the contact info. I will call you the moment we arrive at the airport.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Kinship term used by females.

meanings.en: older male friend or colleague (used by a female)
meanings.note: Commonly used in Korea to address a close older male acquaintance or coworker.

examples.trans: I have one older brother.
Oppa, do you have time right now?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken contraction of 이것.

examples.trans: How much is this?
Please look at this.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Compound of lunch and time.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

examples.trans: This is my father's car.

meanings.note: Used as casual question (치워?).

meanings.note: intransitive verb; also means 'to ride' in another sense

examples.text: 불을 줄이지 않으면 고기가 다 타요.
examples.trans: If you don't lower the heat, the meat will burn completely.

examples.text: 나한테 꼬인 걸 이런 식으로 풀면 안 되지.
examples.trans: You shouldn't take your frustration with me out on her like this.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 풀다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (take out, vent).

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 오늘 내일 잡힌 방송이랑 행사 취소한 것만 열 건이야.
examples.trans: Just the broadcasts and events I canceled for today and tomorrow come to ten.
Here the word for 'events' is key.
My office is close to home.
I go to work at the office at 9 a.m.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean noun; 회의를 하다 means 'to hold a meeting'.

examples.trans: There is a meeting at four in the afternoon.
Please prepare the meeting materials in advance.
I understand well (far, much).
Today is a (far, much) busy day.
